title: Specialist findings file (findings-<name>.json)
$comment: `additionalProperties: false` marks the known key set, but validate.py enforces it SOFTLY: an unknown key is stripped with a logged warning before the strict pass, rather than failing the gate closed. A lens that ran must never have its findings discarded over a cosmetic extra key — a model borrowing one key name from another finding vocabulary it knows would otherwise cost the whole review. The one carve-out is at this file's TOP level, where an unknown key holding an object or an array is left in place and still fails closed: `findings` is a top-level key, so a misnamed container there may be the findings themselves and stripping would fabricate an APPROVE. Inside a finding, a strip can never remove an element of the declared `findings` array nor alter a known field, since known keys are never stripped; content the model writes into a slot this format does not have is dropped, with the warning naming the key. Value validation of the known keys stays strict.

infrastructure_failure.description: The specialist's deterministic 'I could not review' signal: set when the pinned merge-base diff itself errored, alongside an empty findings array. validate.py fails the run closed when any specialist file carries a non-empty string value — an empty findings array alone would compute as APPROVE, greening a PR nobody reviewed, and escalation via prose in the specialist's returned summary depends on the orchestrator noticing it. Nullable like every optional sibling: a model's natural null-for-absence must read as absence (no infra report, findings allowed), not trip validation.

then.$comment: infrastructure_failure (as a string with substance — the \S pattern makes empty and whitespace-only strings read as absence, exactly matching validate.py's infrastructure_failure_message(), and a null constrains nothing either) means 'I could not review', so findings alongside it are a self-contradiction — either the review happened or it didn't. Enforcing the scope here keeps the channel from discarding a run over a subordinate failure the specialist reviewed through: a file carrying both is rejected by schema with a message naming the contradiction, instead of being read as an infra abort.

file.description: File anchor, or null when the finding has none. The key stays required — the model must state the anchor — but its value may be null, for the same reason `line` may: repo-wide, convention, and architectural findings are properties of the tree rather than of one file, and a schema that rejects the null a model naturally writes would fail the gate closed on exactly the findings that most need a human.

line.description: Line anchor, or null when the finding has none. Null is accepted as well as omission: repo-wide, convention, and architectural findings have no single line, and a schema that rejects the null a model naturally writes would fail the gate closed on exactly the findings that most need a human.

body.description: Elaboration, or null when the finding needs none. The field is optional, so absence is already legal; null is that same absence spelled the way a model writes it, and no consumer reads it as anything but text-or-nothing.

confidence.description: Self-reported confidence in 0..1, or null when the specialist has none to offer. Optional like `body`, nullable for the same reason; no script reads it, so a null costs nothing and a rejected null costs the whole run. The bounds still apply to any number given.
